input.brief: Billing and accounts software for small Indian cafes, built by a cafe owner for his own cafe. It turns the till total into the day's real profit after ingredients, rent and salaries.

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Controls on the sentence
hero.blueprint: A dark flat ground with no logo bar: a 14px wordmark top-left and the single action as an underlined text link top-right, both 28px in. The headline is a two-line sentence, centred, at clamp(96px, 9vw, 150px), line-height 1.0, occupying the middle 64% of the width and sitting slightly above the midline. It is set in a variable font and it is the demonstration. Three small control chips from the product sit on top of the sentence, each about 300 by 80px with the product's true radius, a text label and a numeric readout: one above the first line near its left end, one overlapping the start of the second line, and a two-state switch at the lower right. They are tilted 2 to 4 degrees and filled solid, one step lighter than the ground. Each one works: dragging the first changes the headline's weight through `font-variation-settings`, the second changes its letter-spacing, the third toggles uppercase. Mark each chip's root with data-ui. One supporting sentence at 17px, max 40ch, is centred 72px under the headline. The bottom third of the screen stays empty.
hero.mobile: The sentence stays on two lines at 13.5vw, centred at 38% of the height. The three chips shrink to 200 by 60px and move off the letters: one above the sentence and two side by side beneath it, untilted and still live. The supporting sentence follows at 16px. The wordmark stays top-left and the action link top-right.
hero.headline: A two-line sentence of three to five words, up to about 11 characters per line at 9vw, that still reads when its weight and spacing change.

type.note: An American gothic for headings over a sober transitional serif for reading, the pairing of a newspaper front page. Suits essays, annual reports, archives and finance pages that have real paragraphs.

palette.name: Frost and slate
palette.note: Cool white and one paler blue-grey step hold everything, with type in dark slate instead of black. Teal appears once per screen at most, as the primary button or one small detail beside the product photograph.

photos.title: Fog and quiet
photos.note: misty, muted, minimal landscapes and empty horizons; calm areas for text

photos.alt: Gulls perched on a concrete wall beside a pale still sea
Still blue lake with a faint distant shoreline in haze
Single round hay bale in a field under dense fog
Small boathouse at the end of a jetty on dark water at night

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One card, four fields
sections.blueprint: Four flat colour fields stand side by side across the full viewport, each 25vw wide and 84svh tall, butted together with no gaps; neighbours differ clearly in lightness. The same card from the product (a ticket, an order, a request) appears once in each field at the same height, 38% down, centred, 260px wide at true size, each copy marked data-ui. It is further along every time: bare as it arrives, then with an owner and a due date, then with its checklist half ticked, then closed with its final figure. Along the bottom of each field, 28px in, one clause at clamp(22px, 2vw, 32px) on two lines begins with its order word: 'First it lands here.' 'Then someone takes it.' The heading, two to four words at the same size in the heaviest weight, sits top-left in the first field only. On hover a field's card rises 6px over 150ms.
sections.mobile: The fields stack, each full width and 64svh tall, colours meeting edge to edge. In each: the clause at 24px top-left with 20px margins, then the card at true size, left-aligned, 32px below. The heading sits in the first field above its clause, at 24px in the heaviest weight.

sections.name: One row, three states
sections.blueprint: The product's central row (a task, a transaction, a message, a deploy) is shown three times, one directly beneath the other, in three states: as it arrives, with the pointer on it and its actions revealed, and finished. Each copy is built at true size, 640px wide, with real names, amounts and times, its root marked data-ui; inside it the product's own control borders and radii apply. The copies sit in columns 4–9 with 56px between them and nothing framing them. In columns 1–3, right-aligned and level with each copy, one word at 22px in the soft ink names its state. Columns 10–12 stay empty. The middle copy is live: its checkbox or button works and turns it into the third state. The heading, two to four words at 28–32px, sits on column 4's left edge, 96px above the first copy, with no supporting line.
sections.mobile: Copies stack at full width with 16px margins and stay at true size; a row wider than the screen is cropped at its right end, never shrunk. Each state word sits beneath its copy at 17px in the soft ink, 10px away. 48px separates the three groups. Heading at 26px.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: Staggered fragment cells
sections.blueprint: A three-column grid of six filled cells with 8px gaps, each cell 420–460px tall and filled one tone off the ground, no outlines. Every cell has two parts: a text part (a title at 17px medium and three lines at 15px in the soft ink, 24px padding) and a real fragment of the interface at true size (a control, a menu, a table slice, a swatch strip) docked flush against the opposite edge of the cell and cropped by it. The stagger is the idea: across the first row cells run text-top, fragment-top, text-top; the second row runs the reverse, so fragments form a checkerboard. Fragments differ in shape and size on purpose. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, sits left-aligned above the grid with 56px beneath it and no supporting line.
sections.mobile: One column of cells at their natural height with 6px gaps. Every cell runs text first, fragment second, but fragments alternate between docking to the left edge and the right edge, and they are allowed to run off the side of the cell at true size instead of shrinking.

sections.name: The price, very large
sections.blueprint: One plan, no card. Columns 1–4 hold a heading of two to four words at 28–36px and one paragraph at 17px, top-aligned. Columns 6–12 hold the price as a display figure: numerals at clamp(120px, 16vw, 240px), tight tracking, leading 0.85, with the currency sign at half that size raised to the cap line and the period (per month, once) at 18px beside the last numeral on the baseline. One thing from the page overlaps the numerals by 10–15% of their height: the product photograph, the interface fragment or the motif shape, placed over the top-right of the figure. Beneath the figure, on its left edge, four plain lines at 18px state what is included, one per line, without ticks or bullets, then a single rectangular button. The section is at least 80svh tall with the figure vertically centred.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first, full width. The figure follows at 34vw, flush left, with the overlapping object tucked at its top-right corner at a third of the screen wide. Included lines at 17px and a full-width button close the block.

sections.name: Accordion of filled tiles
sections.blueprint: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
sections.mobile: The heading sits above at 9vw, not sticky. Tiles run full width with 6px gaps, questions at 18px wrapping to two lines, closed height at least 64px. The open tile keeps the accent colour, and answers are set at 16px with 20px padding.

sections.name: First step, already open
sections.blueprint: The page ends with the product's first screen already open. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, 90svh tall. Right, in columns 7–11, vertically centred: the product's own create dialog at true size, 440px wide, root marked data-ui, with its real title ('Name your workspace'), one text field holding an editable, believable example, one two-option segmented choice and its primary button. Inside the fragment the product's conventions apply, including the shadow its dialog normally casts. The field accepts typing, the choice switches, and the primary button is the page's only action: it carries the typed value into sign-up. Left, in columns 1–5, anchored to the bottom with 40px margins: the closing line, two to four words at clamp(56px, 7vw, 112px), leading 0.92, on two lines, and under it one sentence at 17px saying what happens after the button. The upper-left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The closing line leads at 13vw on two lines, top-left, with its sentence beneath at 16px. The dialog follows at full width inside 16px margins, at true size, its primary button 52px tall and full width. The field is at least 84svh; the dialog sits in its lower half.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Dabbit
references.idea: The colour picker demonstrates itself on the page: its loupe sits in the hero reading the site's own background hex, and every feature is shown as a real fragment of the app.
references.hero: Near-black viewport split exactly in half by a one-pixel vertical hairline. Left half: a small chrome four-petal logo top-left at a 40px margin, then two thirds of empty dark, then everything else anchored bottom-left: a one-line 30px medium-weight headline, three lines of grey 18px copy, a light pill button beside an outlined pill, and a tiny note. Right half: a 450px rounded square with a thin iridescent border, the app's loupe, empty except for a centre crosshair dot and a small chip reading the hex of the page's own background. Eight pastel dots and lozenges drift across the top-right like spilled swatches.
references.type: InterVariable only. Headline a modest 30px medium with -0.025em tracking; section heads about 22px; cell titles 15px; body 16px grey. Largest text is 3.3vw. Hierarchy comes from white against grey rather than size; hex values use tabular figures.
references.colour: #141416 #2b2b2e #f4f3f2 #9a9aa0 #f4a48c #d4c6e6 — Charcoal ground, off-white and grey text, no brand accent. All colour comes from the product: pastel swatches, tonal scales, and a thin prismatic edge on the loupe and logo. Neutral-cool.
references.imagery: Live-drawn UI fragments on canvas: swatch strips, eleven-step scales, contrast tables, a Figma plugin panel, each in a slightly lighter rounded panel. A chrome 3D logo and chrome price numerals are the only non-UI images.
references.layout: 40px outer margins; the hero's centre hairline becomes a three-column then four-column hairline grid. No section changes background; rhythm is small eyebrow, heading, grid, repeat. Text sits top-left in every cell.

sections.description: A three-column grid ruled by one-pixel hairlines with no card backgrounds. Each cell is over 400px tall: 15px white title and three lines of grey copy, plus a real UI fragment docked above or below (a swatch history strip, a tonal scale, a contrast table, a ten-by-ten colour matrix). Rows alternate text-over-mock and mock-over-text so the grid staggers. The loupe square from the hero reappears floating across cell boundaries.

A four-column, three-row grid of minor features divided by hairlines. Each item is a 14px title prefixed by a tiny coloured glyph (dot, square, triangle or dash, one shape per column, in the app's pastel colours) and two lines of grey text. No icons, no cards, no hover chrome.

Left third: small grey eyebrow, a 22px heading, one paragraph. Right: the price rendered as huge chrome 3D numerals about 150px tall with the loupe square overlapping them, a tiny qualifier beside, and a plain four-line checklist beneath. No pricing card, no border, no tiers.

Closing block centred on the same dark ground: the chrome four-petal logo enlarged to about 200px, pastel shapes scattered widely around it, a two-line 22px sentence, the same two pill buttons, then a one-line footer with copyright left and seven text links right.

steal: Make the hero demo sample the page itself: the tool reports the site's own background value, proving the product without a screenshot.
Build feature grids from hairlines and real UI fragments instead of bordered cards and icons, alternating text-above and mock-above per row.
Keep the headline small (30px) and anchored bottom-left so the product object, not the slogan, owns the first viewport.

references.name: Uni
references.idea: The product lives in the laptop notch, so the page's navigation is a black notch and the hero is a laptop outline whose notch opens into the app.
references.hero: White page with the hero as a rounded-corner panel inset 24px on all sides, filled with a grainy pastel gradient (pink-peach centre, sky blue down the right edge, orange lower-left). A black pill 300×44px sits top-centre like a laptop notch, holding only the app icon; it is the entire nav. Centred below: a hand-scrawled caps eyebrow, a two-line 48px (3.3vw) headline, two white pill download buttons side by side, one line of tiny grey reassurance. The bottom 40% is a thick black outline of a laptop screen, 960px wide, cropped by the fold, its notch expanded into a dark input bar playing the demo.
references.type: Instrument Sans 500 at 48px with -0.025em tracking for headings; Geist 16px for UI and 12–13px captions. Eyebrows are hand-scrawled marker capitals, irregular and tilted. Only three sizes on the page; the headline is just three times the body.
references.colour: #ffffff #fbdad6 #fce6db #aacbec #f9a070 #000000 — Colour lives only in the hero's grainy pastel gradient; below it the page is white and #fbfbfb with black text. Buttons are near-white pills; the notch is the single black mass.
references.imagery: No photos. A laptop reduced to a thick black rounded outline frames a looping screen recording of the notch UI; eight line icons below. The gradient has visible film grain.
references.layout: Everything on the centre axis. The laptop frame's side strokes continue down the page as hairline rules, so the mockup becomes a 960px content column holding tabs, an icon grid and an FAQ. Three short sections, generous white space, minimal footer.

sections.description: Directly under the device a segmented pill control with three tabs switches the demo. Then a hand-scrawled two-word eyebrow, a centred 32px heading, and a four-by-two grid of thin line icons, each with a two-line 12px centred caption. No cards, borders or backgrounds — just icons on white with about 100px between columns, all inside the hairline-bounded column.

A #fbfbfb band inside the same column. The heading straddles the band's top edge. One rounded, hairline-bordered container holds nine rows separated by hairlines; each row has a 12px medium question at left and a thin plus sign at right. Beneath, a two-line micro footer centred: Roman-numeral year, tiny wordmark, a three-word credit, two legal links.

steal: Shape the navigation like the product's own hardware habitat (here a black notch pill) so the nav itself demonstrates the product.
Extend a device mockup's side strokes down the page as hairline rules so the mockup becomes the content column.
Use a hand-scrawled marker eyebrow above a clean grotesk headline to add one human note to a system-clean page.

references.name: Juggle
references.idea: The headline literally drowns: a flat blue field rises to half height and the lines below the waterline turn from red to submerged navy.
references.hero: Two flat fields: white above, saturated blue below, meeting at exactly half height. A three-line all-caps headline in a black-weight grotesque at 8.4vw is centred across the seam, about 65% of the width, lines nearly touching. The first line sits on white in red-orange; the second is cut by the seam, and its lower half plus the whole third line render dark navy as if under water. Small red logo top-left, a rectangular red button with tracked caps top-right. Near the bottom, one line of white condensed caps names the audience. No image, no sub-paragraph.
references.type: Acme Gothic Black 900 caps at 122px, -0.03em, for the hero only. Section heads use Helvetica Now Display Condensed bold caps around 48 to 70px; body is Helvetica Now 17px; labels are small tracked caps. Roughly a 7:1 headline-to-body jump.
references.colour: #2e2eff #ffffff #ff3b1f #0a0a0a #f5f3ef #020156 — Three flat poster colours each own whole sections: electric blue, red-orange and black, with white and warm off-white for product areas. No tints, no gradients.
references.imagery: Simplified product UI on a cream rounded panel over black with a small video-call window; otherwise flat vector graphics: a pair of blinking eyes, a smiley cut into shuffled square tiles.
references.layout: Full-bleed colour blocks with one message each, mostly centred. Product sections switch to a two-column split on off-white with about 90px margins. Marquee strips separate blocks and a slim sticky bar carrying the CTA rides the bottom edge.

sections.description: Full-screen electric blue. Centred stack: a tiny tracked caps label, three lines of white condensed bold caps at about 5vw, a gap, then a single heavier, wider word at a larger size as the punchline, a faint blurred line of text beneath it and an outlined rectangular button. Wide empty margins left and right.

Problem check on full-screen red-orange, under a white marquee strip of condensed caps with small red buttons repeating inside it. Centre: a two-line white condensed caps heading at about 5vw; below, a flat illustration of two white almond eyes with black pupils; a tracked caps instruction line; then three evenly spaced white outlined checkboxes, each with a two-line caption, one already ticked.

Black section. A small tracked caps title centred, under it three numbered text tabs in a row with the active one underlined. Below, a cream rounded app window about 55% wide fills the rest of the viewport: mostly blank note area, a floating status chip, and a small dark video-call window with three faces overlapping its lower edge.

White. Left: a narrow column of small body text, two founder names with roles, then three link columns under tracked caps labels. Right: a blue square about 280px holding a white smiley face sliced into a three-by-three grid of tiles that are rotated and shuffled like a sliding puzzle. Tiny logo and copyright bottom-left.

steal: Split the hero into two flat colour fields and recolour the headline where it crosses the seam, so the layout acts out the copy.
Give each section one saturated flat colour and one sentence, and separate them with a thin marquee strip.
Turn a pain-point list into a mock checklist with real checkboxes under a blunt question heading.
